sentences.text: Herugavialis was a marine gavialoid crocodilian that lived during the Eocene Lutetian stage in what is now the Mokattam Formation of Egypt.
Unlike any living crocodilian, Herugavialis lacked a maxilla process within its lacrimal gland.
Its genus name alludes to the Egyptian god Horus and the missing nose of the Great Sphinx, referencing the absent premaxilla in the holotype skull.
In 2026 the species was transferred to the newly erected genus Herugavialis by Burke and colleagues.
CT scans show that the orbits (eye sockets) are telescoped, a diagnostic trait of Herugavialis cairensis that likely enhanced its visual field.
Phylogenetic analysis places Herugavialis within Gavialidae, indicating a closer relationship to the modern gharial than to the false gharial.
A table of ages lists Herugavialis as occurring in the Middle Miocene.

The authors suggest that Miocene warming may have triggered a temporary resurgence of gavialoid diversity before their eventual disappearance in the Late Miocene, possibly linked to the Messinian Salinity Crisis.
